auditor_check.evidence: review-run.mjs:705 writes a CLI seat's phase1 brief to <run>/phase1/<role>/brief.txt (dispatchDir, :417-419), while build-report.mjs:1356 loadRun reads only <run>/phase1/brief-A.txt, so briefText is null for a CLI first seat and build-report.mjs:702 falls back to the packet. Executed buildReport in memory with a packet hypothesis worded 'Confirm it is fixed' without the definition and both seats answering CONFIRMED: briefText null -> report contains REFUTED plus the flip caveat; briefText defining 'CONFIRMED (the defect it names exists)' -> no REFUTED. Same in both skills' byte-identical copies.

evidence: CLI-seat brief path at review-run.mjs:705 vs loadRun brief-A.txt-only read at build-report.mjs:1356; buildReport with briefText null flips CONFIRMED to REFUTED
Two fixture run folders: brief at phase1/brief-A.txt gives verdict confirmed; brief at phase1/A/brief.txt gives fixWorded true, outcomes REFUTED, one flip caveat
findings.summary: The round-2 polarity fix only finds the seat brief for a native first seat; with a CLI first seat (any Codex/OpenCode seat A, every two-OpenAI pair-review run) the report falls back to the packet and shows a defect-side CONFIRMED as a green REFUTED when the packet lacks the definition sentence.
findings.recommended_fix: In loadRun (build-report.mjs:1356, both copies) read the first existing of phase1/brief-A.txt, phase1/A/brief.txt, phase1/brief-B.txt, phase1/B/brief.txt; add a loadRun test with the CLI layout.

auditor_check.evidence: Ran the shipped whereInChange with a diff map holding aa/src/utils.py (added line 11) and b/src/utils.py (added line 301): 'src/utils.py:11' -> {tag:'added lines'} with no byName; 'src/utils.py:301' -> {tag:'changed file'} with no byName although line 301 is added in the other copy; 'utils.py:11' -> {tag:'unknown', byName:true, addedInOne:true}. Cause: build-report.mjs:633 byPath keeps every suffix match and :638 reduces to the longest path instead of the agree-or-unknown rule used for name matches at :640-644. In this repository the shared scripts are byte-identical, so both copies give the same tag here; the wrong tag needs same-suffix files whose hunks differ.

evidence: whereInChange: longer path holding the added line -> 'added lines' overriding a pre-existing note; shorter path holding it -> 'changed file', blocker moved to Pre-existing with no caveat; bare name -> 'unknown' byName

Two copies plugins/a/scripts/x.mjs and plugins/b/scripts/x.mjs: 'scripts/x.mjs:11' -> 'added lines' no byName; 'scripts/x.mjs:501' -> 'changed file' no byName; 'x.mjs:11' -> 'unknown' byName addedInOne
findings.summary: A folder-qualified partial path that is a suffix of two or more changed files is resolved to the longest path as an exact match, so the Where tag and the pre-existing grouping depend on an arbitrary pick while the bare file name of the same location is handled as a guess.
findings.recommended_fix: In whereInChange (build-report.mjs:638, both copies), when byPath holds more than one distinct path, apply the name-branch rule: tags agree -> that tag with byName true, else 'unknown' with byName and addedInOne; add both orderings to the 'where in the change' test.

auditor_check.evidence: No script reads previous-run.json (grep of both plugins), but build-recheck-packet.mjs:477-478 keeps the previous run path out of the packet on purpose and both SKILL.md files tell the orchestrator that previous-run.json next to the packet records it; the stdout line at :488 is not persisted and, when the record already exists, prints 'not recorded' instead of the path. Removing the file loses the only on-disk link from a packet to the run it re-reviews, so the AC-7 no-loss condition is not met.

evidence: grep previous-run: written at build-recheck-packet.mjs:483-489, documented in --help:53 and SKILL.md in both skills, tested; no reader; stdout at :491 prints the same path
findings.summary: previous-run.json has no script reader, but it is the documented, persisted record of the previous run path for the orchestrator, so removing it is a loss.
findings.recommended_fix: No change needed; optionally have chainRound read it so the record is also used by code.
